expected.summary: pricing stopped quoting prices in euros twelve minutes before the anchor. pricing-1 refreshes FX rates from rates.example.com every five minutes; from sixty seven minutes before the anchor every refresh has failed with 401 invalid_api_key, the provider having revoked the key pricing uses (fxk_live_...7Qd), and pricing kept serving the rates it fetched seventy two minutes before the anchor, logging a WARN on each failed refresh. pricing refuses to quote on rates older than its max_age of 60 minutes, so once the last good rates were an hour old every quote for an eu-west-1 request fails at once with 500 StaleRatesError: fx rate EUR/USD older than max_age 60m, refusing to quote. us-east-1 and us-west-2 quote in USD and are unaffected. About a fifth of GET /search, GET /product/{id}, GET /cart and POST /checkout requests fail, the eu-west-1 share, and the failures propagate through search, checkout, web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. pricing's latency, stores and version did not change and nothing shipped; the hour of WARN lines before the failures is the early sign. promo's nightly promo-expiry-sweep cron, which ran four minutes before the failures began, is routine and unrelated: promo stays error-free.
contributingFactors: rates.example.com rejecting the revoked FX API key on every refresh for an hour
pricing's 60 minute max_age on FX rates, refusing non-USD quotes once the last good rates aged out
every eu-west-1 request needing a EUR quote

criteria.description: Does the brief name the failing FX rates refresh, rates.example.com rejecting a revoked API key for an hour, as the trigger, with pricing's 60 minute max_age then refusing every eu-west-1 quote and the failures reaching edge-gateway? 5 = the refresh failures, the staleness guard, the eu-west-1 segment and the victim chain. Saying only that pricing fails EU quotes, or blaming a pricing store or the promo sweep, scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in the StaleRatesError on pricing spans, the failures confined to eu-west-1, and the WARN refresh failures on pricing-1 starting about an hour before the first error? Cap at 3 unless it explains why the failures began an hour after the refreshes started failing.
Does it avoid blaming the promo-expiry-sweep, a pricing deploy, a pricing store, eu-west-1 traffic or edge-gateway?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
